gen_risks.description: Delay in developing the internal CRM minimum-viable product by November 2025 could impair the expression of interest process for Cohort 1 schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize core functional requirements for the MVP release by November 2025 and establish manual backup processes for school engagement.
gen_risks.evidence: develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Transition of existing National School Breakfast Programme schools may result in delivery gaps when NSBP closes in July 2026 before September 2026 FBC launch.
gen_risks.mitigation: Guarantee places for all 1,700+ participating NSBP schools and issue invitations early to ensure seamless onboarding.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

gen_risks.description: Primary schools may experience physical space and estate constraints preventing effective delivery of breakfast clubs for all enrolled pupils.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy technical estate advisers to evaluate spatial limitations and assist affected schools with space mitigation solutions.
gen_risks.evidence: continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

gen_risks.description: Uncertainty in daily turnout and operational costs at individual school levels may create funding deficits or unexpected cost variances.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide £1,000 initial set-up grants combined with standard daily fixed (£25) and variable per-pupil funding allocations.
gen_risks.evidence: evidence-based, but there will always be a level of uncertainty at an individual school level and on a day-to-day basis.

gen_risks.description: Delays or withholding of timely budget approval and confirmation from HM Treasury could disrupt ongoing rollout and expansion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain rigorous analytical modelling, present evidence from early adopters, and engage early with HM Treasury via project board governance.
gen_risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on several factors. These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury

gen_risks.description: Shortages in skilled personnel within DfE or participating schools could impede program execution and club supervision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure external specialist support advisers through established commercial frameworks and pilot call-centre operational assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

gen_risks.description: Delays in passing or enacting the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could undermine the statutory foundation for mandatory school delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Drive voluntary engagement through grant incentives and phased onboarding ahead of statutory duty commencement.
gen_risks.evidence: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children

gen_risks.description: Upfront Year 1 operational expenditures incurred before attainment benefits accrue after one year could undermine early cost-benefit metrics.
gen_risks.mitigation: Track and highlight immediate short-term benefits, such as childcare savings and parental workforce participation, alongside longer-term attainment data.
gen_risks.evidence: costs are incurred upfront while attainment benefits only materialise after at least one year.

gen_risks.description: Historical funding complexity based on disadvantage levels may confuse mainstream school leaders and decrease willingness to participate.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a simplified, predictable funding model with flat daily rates and clear per-pupil allocations.
gen_risks.evidence: variation by disadvantage levels was deemed to be complicated for mainstream schools, resulting in confusion.

gen_risks.description: Onboarding approximately 2,000 schools across two cohorts within Year 1 may exceed program administrative and operational capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy a hybrid delivery model combining internal DfE capacity with external specialist advisers and funded local authority support.
gen_risks.evidence: combining in-house capability with contracted specialist support to assist onboarding of around 2,000 schools over 2 cohorts.

gen_risks.description: Lack of alignment with broader government programs or local authority initiatives could lead to operational friction and fragmented service delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated funding to local authorities to support system integration and maintain multi-layered governance across government missions.
gen_risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on several factors... alignment with other government programmes

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
